title: Camping feels like the coolest feature they've added in a long time...
author: Yenii_3025
selftext:
This is so fking sad. Look how low gamers standards have fallen.  
  
  
 I can't wait for AI make me look forward to gaming releases.

comments.author: Cole-Thomas52
comments.body: i get the criticism of modern gaming but i don't think people enjoying a camping feature means their standards are low sometimes little things that make a game world feel more alive are exactly what players want

comments.author: Super_Range45
comments.body: There used to be a time people didn't engage in gameplay at all in MMO's, sometimes hours at a time, and would socialize with one another.

comments.author: PHNTMS_exe
comments.body: This seems like a chill part of the game outside of all the action it provides, it's okay to take a break sometimes and relax/socialize. I don't get the post.

comments.author: Bantis
comments.body:
This is such a dumb post, and all you'll achieve is validating people's opinions against AI. One thing doesn't invalidate the other. It's actually a neat social system they've added, and people like it. Great, it's not for you. What the fuck does it have to do with AI? You could use AI to more easily build experimental features like this too.

It's fine if its not you, but hating on it, and somehow equating that AI is the solution is just so incredibly stupid.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
y'know, there is incredibly valuable game design insight you can learn from this if you leave your judgmental attitude at the door and just try to appreciate the combination of systems, polish and little bits of love that elevate a game from being good to one of the best of all time

EDIT: things that make the WoW camping system great and you can learn from / burglarize for your own game:

\- there are many different and totally valid interaction levels with it. lots of people view it purely mechanically - they sit down, get the buff, and they're off. this is perfectly reasonable. lots of players use it socially, or use it just to relax, or use it for comedy. all of that from one pretty simple and small feature

\- it is a small bit of immersion with basically no cost

\- it is a non-forced opportunity for the player to disengage with a potentially monotonous or grindy game loop which requires both minimal game development investment and minimal extraneous player engagement

\- it makes a lot of narrative and genre sense

\- it looks pretty

you get all of that stuff from an incredibly minimalistic system. I try to play games people release here every day; most of them are so garbage i just can't bring myself to even post a reply in the thread. WoW does, with one simple and elegant system, something that most people here cannot do with a hundred bloated and over-scoped systems
